topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text: The old place hums with half-remembered scents. Here, where I move slowly, a soft, familiar shape catches my eye, beckons. Fingers, without thought, trace the worn spots, the threadbare fur that whispers of days long folded into time’s deep pockets. This companion, silent and steadfast, held close in the high drama of play, in the quiet just before sleep. Now, here it rests, amidst the clutter of lives let go, a silent sentinel of simpler days. In the quiet, a thread of past weaves through the present, gentle and unspoken.
